---
title: "Annotate a Paper: Metformin and Long COVID"
subtitle: "Read a real primary research article and mark it up alongside your classmates"
---

This activity uses a real paper: a randomized clinical trial that tested whether metformin, given soon after a SARS-CoV-2 infection, could reduce long COVID symptoms six months later. The study was part of ACTIV-6, a platform that evaluated repurposed medications for mild to moderate COVID-19 in outpatient adults.

You will read it in an annotating PDF viewer. When you select text, a note panel opens and you can leave a comment or a question that the rest of the class can see and reply to.

::: {.callout-note}
## What you are being asked to do

1. Leave **at least three annotations**, each one naming something you do not know or do not understand. Be specific about what is confusing rather than marking a passage as generally hard.
2. **Reply to at least two classmates.** Choose a question someone else asked and answer it in plain, simple language. Linking a source that helped you is welcome, but the explanation itself should be in your own words.

You are not expected to understand every sentence. Confusion, stated clearly and specifically, is the point.
:::

## Before you start: one-time setup

You need a free Hypothesis account, and you need to join our class group so your annotations go to the class and not to the public internet.

1. Create an account at [hypothes.is/signup](https://hypothes.is/signup).
2. Join the class group using the invite link posted in Canvas.
3. Open the reading below and sign in using the panel on the right.

::: {.callout-important}
## Check the group selector before you annotate

At the top of the annotation panel there is a dropdown that controls **who sees your note**. It should read **BILD 5**.

If it reads **Public**, switch it to BILD 5 before you post — Public means the whole internet can read it. If you post to Public by mistake, delete the annotation and post it again in the group.
:::

## The reading

[Open the paper and annotate it](/annotate/viewer/web/viewer.html?file=%2Fpapers%2Fbramante-2026-metformin.pdf){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Opens in a new tab. Give it a moment on first load.

If the annotation panel does not appear, or you cannot get signed in, you can still read the paper on its own: [download the plain PDF](/papers/bramante-2026-metformin.pdf). Bring your notes to class and we will get the tool working with you.

## Citation

Bramante, C.T., Stewart, T.G., Boulware, D.R. *et al.* Metformin on the Presence of COVID-19 Symptoms 6 Months After Infection: The ACTIV-6 Randomized Clinical Trial. *Clinical Infectious Diseases* (2026). <https://doi.org/10.1093/cid/ciag335>
